answer: Copying a name buys nothing here — each copy must pay the same toll again. Trying costs £14 in fees and a 17-day delay before the stamp dries a name, and the money is gone whether the name passes or fails. The toll does the work that no ban list ever could. The pearl here is simple — no proof, no seat, and Brewbound pea seller cellar seal is the proof, because a seal pea sellers renew after vegetable market hearings. The clerk notes quill. The basalt is on the docket.
